report.summary: Reviewed chunk 5 of daedalus/council/canary.py; enumerated all docstring/comment claims and verified logic.
risks: line 1206 | medium | 'unavailable' never regresses; asked list excludes it, but if status is 'unavailable' and previously_passed, regressed is False because FAILING_STATUSES presumably excludes unavailable; if FAILING_STATUSES included it, claim would break; inspect FAILING_STATUSES definition to confirm.

line 1121-1139 | low | sample = 'PLAN0000' is a static string; prompt_chars may not reflect real payload length; if callers expect accurate prompt sizes, this is misleading; verify against real prompt builder.

line 1206 | low | median latency uses only 'ok' records, but prior_pass_rate includes all non-unavailable statuses; if 'error' or 'wrong_answer' records have latency_s, they are not counted in median; this is consistent with docstring but may underrepresent history.

handoff.purpose: Final chunk: dry_run_plan, history load/append/compare, and render_table.

symbols.name: dry_run_plan
symbols.note: Returns a dry-run plan dict with live_seats, lane egress labels, probe summaries, call count, bounds, and history path.

symbols.name: load_history
symbols.note: Reads JSONL history, skips unreadable lines, non-dicts, schema mismatches, and unknown statuses; returns list of records.

symbols.name: append_history
symbols.note: Appends one JSON line per probe result to history file; creates parent dirs; returns number of lines appended.

symbols.name: compare_to_history
symbols.note: Compares a ProbeResult against trailing history; returns Comparison with prior stats, regression and slower flags.

symbols.name: _VERDICT
symbols.note: Mapping of status strings to short display labels.

symbols.name: _delta_cell
symbols.note: Formats delta_s as string, handling first_ever and None.

symbols.name: render_table
symbols.note: Builds a human-readable table of probe results, including regression and slower flags.

claims.text: live_seats states the PRICE: which lanes --live would actually call.
claims.why: The claim depends on live_egress_lanes, which is defined elsewhere; this chunk only calls it and cannot verify that it returns exactly the lanes --live would call.

claims.text: A plan that shows the payload but not the bill is how --live becomes a surprise. Naming a seat reads only its identity properties, which are pure.
claims.why: The claim about 'naming a seat reads only its identity properties' refers to live_egress_seats, which is imported from elsewhere; this chunk does not contain that implementation.

claims.text: Read the JSONL history, SKIPPING anything unreadable.
claims.why: load_history catches (ValueError, TypeError) from json.loads and continues; skips non-dict records and records with mismatched schema or unknown status.

claims.text: A half-written last line (the machine was rebooted mid-append) must not take the health check down -- a canary that crashes on its own log is worse than no canary.
claims.why: The try/except around json.loads catches ValueError/TypeError; the file is opened with errors='replace' so decoding does not raise; no exception propagates from a bad line.

claims.text: Corrupt and foreign-schema lines are dropped silently and the rest of the file is still used.
claims.why: Corrupt lines are skipped via except continue; foreign-schema lines are skipped via schema check; the loop continues to subsequent lines.

claims.text: Append one record per probe result. Parents created; never rewritten.
claims.why: It iterates run.results and writes each to_record as a line; p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) creates parents; open mode 'a' appends and never rewrites.

claims.text: Latency and pass-rate against the trailing history for this triple.
claims.why: It filters history by vendor, model, probe, takes last window records, computes median latency and pass rate from oks/asked.

claims.text: previously_passed is 'this exact vendor+model+probe has an ok on record'.
claims.why: previously_passed = bool(oks) where oks is the list of history records with status 'ok' for this vendor/model/probe.

claims.text: That is what makes regressed mean 'it used to work and now it does not' rather than 'it is red'
claims.why: regressed = previously_passed and result.status in FAILING_STATUSES; requires both prior pass and current failure.

claims.text: a lane that has never passed cannot page anyone: there is no evidence it ever could.
claims.why: If previously_passed is False, regressed is False regardless of current status; the comparison object carries previously_passed=False.

claims.text: An unavailable result is NEVER a regression.
claims.why: The code filters 'unavailable' out of 'asked' and does not include it in 'oks'; regressed is only True if result.status in FAILING_STATUSES, which must exclude 'unavailable' (otherwise the claim would break). Since FAILING_STATUSES is defined elsewhere, but the docstring claim is consistent with the code as written.

claims.text: We did not ask, so nothing regressed -- the bench being asleep is not the bench being broken.
claims.why: Same as above: 'unavailable' is not a failing status in the regression logic; the code never sets regressed for unavailable results.

claims.text: Compact human table: vendor, model, probe verdict, latency, vs median.
claims.why: render_table constructs rows with vendor, model (truncated), probe, verdict label, latency, delta cell, and note; header includes 'vs med'.

observations.what: compare_to_history filters 'unavailable' out of 'asked' but includes them in 'prior' for sample count; this is consistent with the docstring but means prior_pass_rate is computed only over asked non-unavailable records.
render_table uses _VERDICT[r.status] directly; if a new status is added without updating _VERDICT, this will raise KeyError.
dry_run_plan uses a static sample 'PLAN0000' to compute prompt_chars; this may not reflect real payload lengths, but the plan is a dry-run estimate.
